title: Qualitative Characterization of the Aqueous Fraction from Hydrothermal Liquefaction of Algae Using 2D Gas Chromatography with Time-of-flight Mass Spectrometry
protocol: Generate a mixed aqueous/organic product stream via continuous flow HTL of algae according to published procedures.
Separate the product stream into an aqueous phase and organic phase using a gravity separator.
Filter 10 ml of the HTL aqueous phase with a 0.45 µm syringe filter.
Store filtered samples in a refrigerator at 4 °C for GC × GC–TOF-MS analysis.
Use a gas chromatograph equipped with a quad-jet dual stage cooling-based modulator and time-of-flight mass spectrometer for experiments.
Configure the auto-sampler to inject 1 µl of each sample or standard into the GC.
Utilize a randomized block design for sample and standard injections as described in literature.
Cut both edges of primary and secondary columns straight without sharp edges before connecting.
Place ferrule on the GC column and connect primary column to the GC injector with 5 mm of column inside.
Ensure that glass liner, non-stick liner O-ring and septa for GC injector are new and free of contamination.
Use 1/16 x 0.5 mm ID transfer line ferrules to connect the secondary column and transfer line.
Place a 0.2 m portion of the secondary column in the transfer line.
Ensure that a 0.1 m portion of the secondary column is in the modulator.
Use ultrahigh purity helium gas as carrier gas for GC at a flow rate of 1.5 ml min-1.
Ensure there is sufficient liquid nitrogen in the Dewar which acts as a coolant in the modulator.
Predict the level of liquid nitrogen using a pressure gauge attached to its outlet.
Set-up the quality control (QC) method and run in-built 'acquisition system adjustments' protocol to achieve maximum signal response using manufacturer's protocol.
Run in-built 'instrument optimization' protocols of QC method, in series - filament focus, ion optic focus and mass calibration tests using manufacturer's protocol.
Ensure that mass calibration test passes.
Perform a leak check using the manufacturer's protocol.
Analyze the automatically generated leak check report.
Ensure that the relative concentration of N2 (ion 28), O2 (ion 32), and moisture (ion 18) is below 10%, 3%, and 5% respectively, compared to the internal standard mass spectra of ion 69.
Tune the TOF-MS using the manufacturer's protocol.
Run a quality control method before and after performing the leak check and while analyzing samples and standards.
Arbitrarily select a long modulation period (e.g., 10 seconds or 13 seconds).
Inject a sample as described in step 2.2.
Identify the retention time in the second dimension of the contour plot after which no peaks elute.
Select the identified second dimension retention time as the optimum modulation period.
Increase the modulation period and perform the analysis again if "wrap around" is observed.
Repeat steps 4.2 and 4.3 until the optimum value is determined.
Install a polar capillary column as the primary column.
Bake the primary column for at least 2 hours to remove moisture, air, and contaminants.
Install a non-polar capillary column as the secondary column.
Bake the secondary column for at least 2 hours to remove moisture, air, and contaminants.
Use ultrahigh purity helium gas as carrier gas for GC at a flow rate of 1.5 ml/min.
Set the GC injector temperature to 260 °C.
Set the split ratio to 1:250.
Maintain the primary column temperature at 40 °C for 0.2 min.
Ramp the primary column temperature to 260 °C at a rate of 5 °C/min.
Maintain the primary column temperature at 260 °C for 5 min.
Set the modulator temperature 5 °C higher than that of the secondary column.
Set the secondary column temperature 5 °C higher than that of the primary column.
Use an optimum modulation period of 4 seconds with a hot pulse of 0.8 seconds and a cold pulse of 1.2 seconds.
Set the transfer line temperature to 270 °C.
Set the acquisition delay or solvent delay to 0 seconds.
Set the lower range of m/z to 35.
Set the higher range of m/z to 800.
Set the MS detector acquisition rate at 400 spectra/sec.
Maintain the MS detector voltage at 150 V higher than the optimized value.
Maintain the MS ion source temperature at 225 °C.
Perform data processing using the software supplied by the instrument manufacturer.
Select the task to compute baseline in the data analysis method.
Find peaks above the baseline.
Conduct a library search to identify compounds.
Calculate area/height for identified peaks.
Track the baseline through the entire data file.
Enter baseline offset as 0.5.
Enter expected peak width of 15 seconds in the first dimension.
Enter expected peak width of 0.15 seconds in the second dimension.
Set signal-to-noise ratio to 5,000 for compound identification.
Set similarity values greater than 850 for accurate compound identification.
Select a commercially available mass spectral library for compound identification.
Set the library search mode to forward.
Process data files using the manufacturer's protocol.
